text:
River of the Seven Stars,

path of the Liberator,

blood of the Heart of America,

aorta that does not leave the heart!


Thin river of the springs,

angry river of the falls,

river of the seven stars,

that at the Source do not fill the hollow of the hands

and then become the dream of a sea without restraint!


Bewitching river, that paints yourself with every sky,

River of La Urbana, pampas plain,

River of San Félix, solution of glory,

River of Angostura, channel of war,

River of Barrancas, River of thinking

how there can be so much water on Earth,

River of our Hope,

when Hope shall be!

River of us, our very mirror,

mirror of this soul of ours,

through which, tireless as you are for horizons,

we sweat through twists and turns!

I shall not lay my hands upon your back,

I shall not paint your banks,

for if on the left you have the heart of the cities,

on the right you raise the arm of the forests;

I shall not touch your waters, your millions of drops,

which are the tithe of the peaks for the worship of the prairies,

I shall not walk upon your waves,

for the Master will come walking upon them.


I only want to widen my eyes

toward the future procession sailing upon your waters

and toward the procession of the past,

toward reality and promise,

toward Antonio Díaz's boat

and toward the deep dream in which you dream

of the prow of the battleship,

as peasant children dream of their string steamboat,

of the steel ship

that will advance toward your springs haloed with sails,

and with the rainbow's dove standing at the masthead,

its breast opened by your Seven Stars…

translation.title: The Future Boat
translation.editorial_note: The source contains a stray “P>” marker before “No he de poner”; it is removed from the English and the paragraph break it interrupted is restored, documented here as an OCR artifact.
